findings.where: the note at the foot of the thread, under the 'noor writing…' line — x 62-772, y 1431-1780 of the 1080x2340 frame, about 12% of the screen; present in 207 of 256 frames (80.9%), app time 0.05 s to 4.08 s, including the final frame
findings.what: The composing/incoming note is a flat off-white card with a drop shadow: its left edge sits at column x=62 with a standard deviation of 0.00 px over 320 rows and its top edge on rows 1429-1430 with a standard deviation of 0.49 px over 680 columns, its fill is RGB (242.6, 237.2, 228.1) with a high-pass texture standard deviation of 1.27 grey levels against 12.69 for the real note two positions above it in the same frame, and a soft shadow falls off to the right from 236 to 104 over eight pixels.
findings.why: The anti-goal names this exact shape — 'a beige rounded rectangle with a drop shadow' — as a failure of the entire visual concept, and this surface is an approximation of paper rather than a photograph of it, ten times flatter than the notes beside it and cut to a mathematically straight rectangle where every other note in the evidence carries a torn edge.

findings.where: the same placeholder card, x 61-776, y 1786-1944, in 31 of 502 frames (6.2%) — two runs at app time 2.42-2.67 s and 3.60-3.81 s
findings.what: The same flat rectangle appears again: bounding-box fill 0.9898, interior standard deviation 2.92 grey levels, four straight edges, square corners, a drop shadow at the bottom and right, and no tear, no rule, no ink.
findings.why: It is the same forbidden shape recurring on a second clip, so it is a property of the composing state rather than one bad frame, and simulated paper is scored twice by design.

findings.where: the 'read' list of 115 strings, set against 13_messenger_states.png (the reply strip above the composer) and 03_us.report.json (view.modules[].glance)
findings.what: The sweep reports findings: [] but does not cover every string the app puts on screen — 13_messenger_states.png displays 'answering state_declared', a raw internal identifier, and the phrase 'state_declared' occurs nowhere in strings.json; three of the five module glance lines the Us surface composes ('last: tuesday soup', 'us in 63 days', 'waiting on you: the one you said you stopped') are likewise absent from the 115 entries.
findings.why: The clean voice result is a linter's claim over a subset, not a proof over the displayed text, and the one nudge-shaped phrase anywhere in the evidence — 'waiting on you: the one you said you stopped' — is exactly the kind of string the no-guilt anti-goal exists to catch, yet it is neither swept nor rendered anywhere a reader could judge it.

findings.where: the Us surface, which runs DATES, AHEAD, BEEN, TO DO, OPEN and then ends at the todos list; and the missing Android setup shot
findings.what: The rituals module — the one place engagement machinery would live — is never rendered in any artifact, although 03_us.report.json records it as present with 53 events and the glance 'last: tuesday soup'; 16_setup_android.png is absent with the reason 'not captured this session', which is where the Android setup copy would be read.
findings.why: Compliance on the streak-and-guilt anti-goal rests on a linter rule scoped to 'files whose path contains ritual' rather than on a picture of the surface, and a rubric row that asks whether a forbidden interpretation appears anywhere cannot be closed out on a surface the evidence never shows.

what_is_working: No emoji glyph appears anywhere in the evidence. The emotional layer is 36 named feelings (evidence/crops/haptics_strip.png) carried by rendered physical objects with cast shadows — bunting for 'yes', a folded paper hat, a rubber band for 'snap', a row of staples for 'stuck with me', a leaf cluster for 'nuzzle' — drawn from 501 objects built by 129 recipes with no problems reported (evidence/logs/recipes.json). Nothing in 01_pulse.png, 15_authored_feeling.mp4 or 07_feeling_landing.mp4 is a glyph or a piece of clip art standing in for a feeling.

The voice holds across every string I could read on screen. Ten stills and five clips carry no exclamation mark, no 'Oops', no 'get started', and the reader is never called a user. Errors read 'can't reach the other phone. it'll go when it can.'; the media viewer's dismiss reads 'PUT IT BACK'; the empty list reads 'nothing to do. suspicious.'

The app never names itself. evidence/logs/pwa.json records the served manifest name as 'the other phone', so even the home-screen label avoids a product name, and no header, tab or setup step in any artifact carries one.

No engagement machinery is visible on any rendered surface. The only counts on screen are functional — 'TO DO / 10 open' in 03_us.png, '0:47' on a voice note — and the rituals glance the app composes is 'last: tuesday soup', a memory rather than a run length. There are no badges, points, levels, progress rings or streak warnings in any of the fifteen artifacts.

Away from the placeholder, the paper is not simulated. Across ten stills my detector for an axis-aligned near-uniform bright rectangle (bounding-box fill above 0.985, wider than 300 px, taller than 80 px) returns nothing at all, and the same detector finds nothing in 07_feeling_landing.mp4, 11_chat_scroll.mp4 or 15_authored_feeling.mp4. Real notes carry irregular torn contours (evidence/logs/tears.json: 8 visible, 8 distinct, no repeats, from a pool of 56), and ten clean paper interiors sampled from 02_chat.png cross-correlate at a median of 0.005 and a maximum of 0.30 after high-pass filtering, so the mottle is aperiodic rather than a tiled or procedurally repeated overlay.
verdict: Three of the four anti-goals are met cleanly and I can show it with numbers: no emoji glyph anywhere, 36 feelings carried by rendered objects rather than symbols, a voice that never exclaims, never says 'user' and never names the app (its own manifest calls it 'the other phone'), and no badge, point, level or streak on any rendered surface. The fourth fails in one specific place. The note the app shows while a message is being composed or is arriving is a flat off-white rectangle with a drop shadow: in 06_unfolding.mp4 its left edge is constant to 0.00 px over 320 rows and its top edge varies by 0.49 px over 680 columns, its interior carries 1.27 grey levels of texture against 12.69 for the torn, ruled note two positions above it in the same frame, and it is on screen for 207 of 256 frames including the last one, with the same card returning for 31 frames of 08_state_propagating.mp4. That is the anti-goal's named shape, in the app's own timeline, next to the real thing that shows how much better the rest of the surface is — and the rubric puts this failure here as well as under material truth on purpose. Two smaller gaps keep the rest from being fully closed out: the 115-string sweep that reports no findings does not contain 'answering state_declared', which 13_messenger_states.png puts on screen, nor three of the five module glance lines the Us surface composes, one of which reads 'waiting on you: the one you said you stopped'; and the rituals module, the single most likely home for engagement machinery, is recorded in 03_us.report.json but never rendered in any artifact, so its compliance is asserted by a path-scoped lint rule rather than shown. Score 7.5 of 10, below the floor of 9, and the whole of the shortfall would be recovered by giving the composing note the same paper, tear and texture every other note in the build already has.
